- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate early in horizon; reduce forecast for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.50), model underestimates; increase forecast for first 3–5 days, especially if recent price is volatile.
- Model consistently overpredicts spikes in sentiment-driven rallies (e.g., 2025-03-31, 2025-04-01) — cap forecast at 2x recent high if sentiment >0.67.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods after sharp spikes — add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag — add 0.05–0.15 to forecast for last 5–7 days to catch momentum.
- If sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) for 3+ days, model underperforms — increase forecast by 0.05–0.10 for last 3–5 days to avoid underestimation.
